name: Successive overrelaxation stationary solver
definition: For A=D+L+U solve (D+ωL)x_(k+1)=ωb+[(1−ω)D−ωU]x_k with fixed relaxation ω.
variables: D diagonal; L,U strict triangular parts; ω relaxation; x iterate
assumptions: Nonzero diagonal; symmetric positive definite A and 0<ω<2 suffice for convergence in exact arithmetic.
limitations: Ordering and relaxation affect convergence; ω=1 reduces to Gauss–Seidel.
failure_conditions: Zero diagonal, nonfinite iterate or residual tolerance not met within bound
computation: Sweep relaxed Gauss–Seidel coordinates; check true residual.

source.citation: Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems, §2.2.3, equation (2.7) and Fig. 2.3; lower and upper parts here have opposite signs to the book's convention. https://netlib.org/templates/templates.html

application: General numerical solution of a linear system.
required_inputs: Square matrix, right side, initial iterate, relaxation and stopping bounds.
incompatible_methods: Claiming convergence for arbitrary relaxation and matrices
mechanism_note: A fixed relaxation of the ordered Gauss–Seidel sweep; ω=1 gives the parent iteration exactly. Counted as a variant, not a new distinct algorithm.
